rationale: Both follow the same validation sequence with the same messages. B's length handling is more direct: a single if/elif chain checks the 11-digit, too-short and too-long cases against the original digit count. A strips the country code first and then reports 'greater than 11 digits' by checking for more than 10, which is confusing. B whitelists allowed punctuation explicitly, including any whitespace, and then extracts digits with \D. A's cleanup only removes literal spaces, so a tab would wrongly be reported as punctuation. B's pretty also reuses the area_code property in an f-string. Overall B is slightly clearer and more robust.
